full_judgment:
A. K. M. Abdul Hakim, J: This Rule was issued upon an application under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the informant-petitioner Sk. Mahenul Hoque calling in question an order dated 21.10.2012 passed by the learned Joint Metropolitan Sessions Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Metro Sessions Case No. 7636 of 2012 arising out of Mirpur Model Police Station Case No. 31 dated 13.03.2012 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 196 of 2012 under sections 385/ 506/ 509/ 109 of the Penal Code allowing an application of the accused-opposite parties praying for discharge under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule are that petitioner-Sk. Maherul Hoque as informant lodged first information report with Mirpur Police Station on 13.03.2012 against accused Md. Nazmul Hossain Gazi including accused-Opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 under sections 385/506 of the Penal Code alleging inter alia, that this younger sister, Ms. Monika Pervin is an officer of Eastern Bank Ltd. On 24.112011 at about 01,35 P.M. from mobile phone No. 01716247236 an unknown person made a phone call to the mobile No. 01717697546 of Monika Parvin and threatened to kill her and demanded subscription (Chanda) Ten lac. Thereafter from mobile phone No. 01766777994 and 01766777995 to the mobile number of Monika Pervin one after another message (SMS) were sent demanding Taka Ten lac. Some of the SMS was made and scandalous and pursuant to that she lodged four General Diaries with Mirpur Model Police Station being Nos. (1) 2388 dated 30.11.2011, (2) 142 dated 21.01.2012, (3) 2033 dated 27.02.2012 and (4) 865 dated 11.03.2012. The number from which the message were sent has been used by Md. Nazmul Hossain Gazi. It appears that Nazinul Hossein Gazi and other unknown persons in between 24.11.2011 to 07.03.2012 on different occasions made phone calls and SMS from aforesaid mobile numbers and claimed take ten lac as subscription and threatened to kill her; that having informed the incident and collecting the details of the accused the instant case was lodged. 

 3. On completion of investigation, police submitted charge sheet against the accused-opposite party No. 2 and 3 and another on 28.08.2012 under sections 385/506/509 and 109 of the Penal Code. After submission of the police report the case record was transmitted to the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge, Dhaka and same was registered as Metro Sessions Case No. 7636 of 2012. Thereafter, the case was fixed for framing charge on 21.10.2012 and on that date an application for discharge has been filed by the accused-opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the ground that there is no material allegation against the accused’s-opposite party under sections 385 and 506 of the Penal Code. 

 5. The informant being aggrieved by the impugned order discharging the accused-opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 from the sections case, filed the revisional application under section 439 read with Section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present rule and stay against the order of discharge. 

 7. It is further stated that the informant sister is the divorced wife of Shaikh Joynuddin who long after execution of divorce filed C.R. Case No. 492 of 2011 under section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the proceedings of which has been stayed till disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8311 of 2012. It was also stated that the accused Nazmul Hossain Gazi made statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure did not say anything against the present opposite parties regarding their involvement of the alleged demand of Chanda. Opposite party Nos. 2-3 are not FIR named accused, but maliciously implicated in the instant case on the basis of 164 statement made by the co-accused Nazmul Hossain Gazi. Opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 are full brothers and son of freedom fighter late Sk. Emam Ali Opposite party No.2 Sk. Abdul Goni is Upazilla Education Officer, Dumuria, Khulna and opposite party no.3 is serving as senior Assistant Police Commissioner, Khulna Metropolitan Police, Khulna who has been awarded president Police Medal (PPM) in 2014 for his honest, sincere and courageous performance. 

 8. The petitioner subsequently filed supplementary affidavit dated 02.09.2015 stating that the accused petitioner no.3 Sk. Join Uddin got married with Monika Parvin by registered Nikanama on 02.02.2009 and on the someday he took Taka 50,00,000/- (Taka fifty lac) only as dowry from the victim's brothers. Then on 06.02.2010 allegedly the said Sheikh Joynuddin divorced the victim by sending divorce notice to the victim as well as to the Union Prishad Chairman by registered with A/D vide serial No.355 and 356 dated 14.02.2010 but the fact is that on 17.02.2010 the Union Parishad Chairman received a letter which was sent by said Shikh Joynuddin regarding construction of the road of Khulna to Satkhira and accordingly, the Union Parishad Chairman, Labsha Union, Satkhira registered about the said letter in the letter receiving registry book being serial No.13 dated 17.02.2010 regarding that issued a certificate on 24.03.2010 as per requirement of to brother of the victim Moreover there is no arbitration by the said Union Parishad Chairman regarding their divorce, since the said Chairman did not receive any divorce, since the said Chairman did not receive any divorce notice. It was further stated that said sheikh Joynuddin filed Civil Suit No. 58 of 2013 the Joint District Judge, 2'd Court, Khulna with a prayer for declaration of execution of divorce given on 06.02.2010 by the plaintiff and there has been no relationship with victim Monika parvin and on this suit defendant, Monika Parvin filed an application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for rejection of the plaint since the suit is barred under section 5 of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 and hence the case was not maintainable in the court and the court by order dated 22.01.2014 rejected the said application. Thereafter, the defendant Monika Parvin filed Civil Revision No. 828 of 2014 before this court against the order dated 22.01.2010 passed in Tale suit No. 58 of 2013 by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna and upon hearing the parties the rule was made absolute 15.03.2015 with a direction to the teamed judge to return of the plaint to the plaintiff to submit it to the proper court. 

 10. Mr. Abdul Motin Khoshur, the Learned Senior Advocate for the Petitioner submits that the learned Metropolitan Join Sessions Judge upon serious misconception of law and facts and without giving proper hearing to the parties and applying without judicial mind and other materials on record and the facts and circumstances of the case, most illegality and arbitrarily allowed the application of the opposite-party nos. 2 and 3 under Section 265 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and wrongly discharged the accused’s-opposite parties from the case under Sections 385/506 of the penal code as a result of which there has been miscarriage of justice. He further submits that the learned Metropolitans Joint Sessions judge without applying his judicial mind and totally misread and non-consider the material evidence on record erroneously discharged the accused opposite parties nos. 2-3. 

 11. Mr. A.K.M Faiz with Mr. Md. Mesbahul Islam Asif, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 opposed the Rule. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties that the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge after proper consideration of the materials on record and the facts and circumstances of the case rightly allowed the application of the opposite-parties under Section, 265C of the code of Criminal procedure and discharged the accused-opposite Parties from the case Learned Advocate further submits that no allegation was brought against the opposite-prates in the FIR and their name were not mentioned therein and co-accused Md. Nazmul Hossain Gazi Did not say anything in his 164 statement against the opposite-parties regarding their involvement of the alleged demand of chanda. As such the trial court passed the order correctly recording order of discharge against them. Learned Advocate next submits that the FIR was lodged by brother of the victim Monika Parvin showing date of occurrence on 24.11.2011 but facts remains victim herself filed General Dairy over the said incident on 28.11.2011 in which she did not mention anything about demand of chanda, even in two other subsequent GD filed on 02.12.2011 and 27.02.2012 there is nothing regarding demand of chanda. He also submits that the state did not file the present revisional application though the case being sessions case the state is presumed to be aggrieved party and that this application at the instance of the informant is, therefore, is not maintainable. 

 15. In a criminal case firstly, any allegation either in FIR or in the charge sheet, must constitute an offence within the meaning of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Secondly, the allegation must be based on materials on record and not on mere surmises or suppositions. The process of law must not be used as the engine of harassment. In the present case on a bare reading of FIR, General Dairies and charge sheet it would appear that the facts stated therein clearly and manifestly failed to prove the alleged charge against the opposite parties. 

 16. It appears that the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge after applying his judicial mind and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record particularly the FIR lodged by the petitioner rightly allowed the application of the opposite party after recording its reason under section 265D of the Criminal Procedure. 

 17. Thus having considered all aspect of the matter and submissions advanced by the learned Advocate of both the parties and relevant provision of Section 265D of the Code of Criminal Procedure we hold that the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge on consideration of the materials on record correctly found that there was no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused-opposite party Nos. 2 and 3, consequently discharged the accused from the Sessions Case. 

 18. In view of these facts and circumstances of the case, we do not find that the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge committed any illegality in discharging the accused-opposite party No. 2 and 3 from the aforesaid sections case, and, as such, we do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned order for which the Rule should be discharged.
